Where standing or admissibility is required by the use case, each required property is explicitly and unambiguously represented before consequential reliance.
RequiredEvidence: Governing State Object; authority reference or explicit NOT_ESTABLISHED authority state; applicable standing representation; applicable admissibility representation; use-case applicability criteria; inspection record.
FailureOracle: FAIL if relied-upon authority is absent or silently assumed without an explicit authority reference or NOT_ESTABLISHED state, or if standing or admissibility is required by the use case but is absent, ambiguous or silently inferred.
Notes: Controlled successor definition arising from human semantic review of LILP-REQ-STATE-003 and LILP-REQ-STATE-004. One structural-state test covers the shared explicit-representation gap. Definition existence does not establish requirement mapping, harness binding, execution or conformance.

Title: Material Evidence Object possesses stable identifier
Objective: Establish that each material Evidence Object relied upon by governance possesses an explicit stable evidence identifier.
Preconditions: A material Evidence Object exists in preserved form and is intended to be relied upon by a governance determination or other consequential governance process.
Stimulus: Inspect the Evidence Object identifier and perform repeated read-only references to the same unchanged preserved Evidence Object within the declared scope.
ExpectedSystemBehaviour: The Evidence Object contains a non-empty explicit evidence identifier, and repeated references to the same unchanged preserved Evidence Object resolve to the same identifier within the declared scope.
RequiredEvidence: Material Evidence Object; explicit evidence identifier field or equivalent representation; declared scope; repeated read-only inspection or reference records demonstrating identifier stability.
FailureOracle: FAIL if the material Evidence Object lacks an explicit evidence identifier, the identifier is empty or ambiguous, or the same unchanged preserved Evidence Object resolves to inconsistent identifiers within the declared scope without an explicit permitted identity rule.
Notes: Controlled successor definition arising from human semantic review of LILP-REQ-EVID-001. Stable Evidence Object identity is tested separately from provenance, admissibility and package re-hashability. Definition existence does not establish requirement mapping, harness binding, execution or conformance.

Title: Material evidence class is explicitly represented
Objective: Establish that the evidence class of a material Evidence Object is explicitly represented where different epistemic classes could materially affect the determination.
Preconditions: A material Evidence Object is available for a governance determination and the applicable context permits different epistemic evidence classes whose distinction could materially affect the determination.
Stimulus: Inspect the Evidence Object and the determination context and identify the explicitly represented evidence class relied upon for evidentiary evaluation.
ExpectedSystemBehaviour: Where epistemic class is material to the determination, the Evidence Object explicitly and unambiguously represents its evidence class before the evidence is relied upon.
RequiredEvidence: Material Evidence Object; explicit evidence-class field or equivalent representation; applicable epistemic-class vocabulary or classification rule; determination context; inspection record.
FailureOracle: FAIL if different epistemic classes could materially affect the determination and the relied-upon Evidence Object has no explicit evidence class, has an ambiguous class, or requires the class to be silently inferred from unrelated context.
Notes: Controlled successor definition arising from human semantic review of LILP-REQ-EVID-002. Explicit epistemic evidence-class representation remains distinct from provenance, admissibility and evidence-object identity. Definition existence does not establish requirement mapping, harness binding, execution or conformance.

Title: External evidence payload is bound to integrity identifier
Objective: Establish that where integrity of an external evidence payload is claimed, the payload itself or a verifiable content reference to that payload is explicitly bound to the integrity identifier supporting the claim.
Preconditions: An external evidence payload, or a verifiable reference to that payload, is presented and an integrity claim is made using an identified integrity value or mechanism.
Stimulus: Inspect the external payload or verifiable content reference, the claimed integrity identifier and the representation that binds the payload or reference to that identifier.
ExpectedSystemBehaviour: The integrity identifier is explicitly and unambiguously bound to the external payload or to a verifiable content reference that resolves to the claimed payload, so the integrity claim is attributable to the identified content rather than to an unbound value.
RequiredEvidence: External evidence payload or verifiable content reference; integrity identifier; binding representation; applicable integrity method or metadata; inspection record demonstrating the payload-or-reference relationship.
FailureOracle: FAIL if integrity is claimed but the integrity identifier is detached from the external payload or its verifiable content reference, the binding is absent or ambiguous, or the identifier cannot be attributed to the payload claimed without unsupported inference.
Notes: Controlled successor definition arising from human semantic review of LILP-REQ-EVID-007. Payload-or-reference integrity binding remains distinct from independent package re-hashability. Definition existence does not establish requirement mapping, harness binding, execution or conformance.

Title: Detected material change is represented separately from predecessor state
Objective: Establish that a detected material change is represented as a distinct delta or change record rather than by mutating, replacing or conflating the preserved predecessor state.
Preconditions: A valid predecessor state exists, a successor or candidate state contains a detected material change, and the comparison basis is available.
Stimulus: Compare the predecessor and changed state, detect the material change, and inspect the resulting representation of that change and its relationship to the predecessor state.
ExpectedSystemBehaviour: The detected material change is represented in a distinct Delta Object or equivalent change record that is separately identifiable from the predecessor state, while the predecessor state remains preserved as the predecessor.
RequiredEvidence: Preserved predecessor state; changed successor or candidate state; comparison basis; detected material change; distinct Delta Object or equivalent change record; predecessor and successor references; inspection record.
FailureOracle: FAIL if a detected material change is represented only by mutating, replacing or silently rewriting the predecessor state, or if the change cannot be distinguished as a separate delta representation from the preserved predecessor.
Notes: Controlled successor definition arising from human semantic review of LILP-REQ-DELTA-002. Separate delta representation is distinct from detecting and classifying material change. Definition existence does not establish requirement mapping, harness binding, execution or conformance.

Title: Delta Object identifies affected governing predicates
Objective: Establish that a Delta Object explicitly identifies the governing predicates affected by a material change where the relationship between the change and those predicates can be established.
Preconditions: A valid predecessor state and changed successor or candidate state exist, a material delta has been established, and available evidence permits one or more affected governing predicates to be identified.
Stimulus: Inspect the established Delta Object, comparison evidence and relevant governing predicates and determine which predicates are affected by the material change.
ExpectedSystemBehaviour: Where the relationship can be established, the Delta Object explicitly and unambiguously identifies the affected governing predicates and preserves that relationship as part of the delta representation.
RequiredEvidence: Predecessor and successor or candidate states; Delta Object; changed fields or conditions; applicable governing predicates; evidence supporting the affected-predicate relationship; inspection record.
FailureOracle: FAIL if an affected governing-predicate relationship can be established but the Delta Object omits it, represents it ambiguously, or requires the affected predicates to be silently inferred from unrelated context. FAIL if unsupported affected-predicate relationships are invented as established.
Notes: Controlled successor definition arising from human semantic review of LILP-REQ-DELTA-004. Affected-predicate identification remains distinct from general delta detection and classification. Definition existence does not establish requirement mapping, harness binding, execution or conformance.

Title: Claimed identity continuity is supported by sufficient identity evidence
Objective: Establish that where identity continuity is required or claimed, the claimed link is supported by sufficient identity evidence under the applicable identity method rather than by assertion, naming similarity or unsupported inference.
Preconditions: Two or more governance objects, states or chain positions are presented with a claimed identity-continuity relationship, and the applicable identity method and evidence needed to evaluate that relationship are available.
Stimulus: Inspect the claimed continuity link, the identities of the linked objects or states, the applicable identity method and the identity evidence presented in support of the link.
ExpectedSystemBehaviour: The continuity claim is accepted only where the available identity evidence is sufficient under the applicable identity method to support the claimed link. The supporting evidence and evaluated link remain identifiable and inspectable.
RequiredEvidence: Objects or states participating in the claimed continuity link; stable identifiers or applicable identity material; declared identity or continuity method; identity evidence supporting the link; continuity evaluation record; inspection record.
FailureOracle: FAIL if identity continuity is accepted without sufficient supporting identity evidence, if the claimed link depends only on naming similarity or unsupported inference, or if the evidence supporting the claimed continuity relationship cannot be identified and inspected.
Notes: Controlled successor definition arising from human semantic review of LILP-REQ-CHAIN-002. Positive identity-evidence sufficiency for a claimed continuity link remains distinct from stable object identity, name-based substitution resistance, and failure handling when identity cannot be established. Definition existence does not establish requirement mapping, harness binding, execution or conformance.

Title: Material chain-boundary determination is explicitly recorded
Objective: Establish that where a chain-boundary determination materially affects execution, verification or claim scope, the applicable boundary determination is explicitly recorded rather than left implicit or reconstructed after the affected decision.
Preconditions: A governed examination or decision context contains an identifiable chain boundary whose determination materially affects at least one downstream execution, verification or claim-scope consequence.
Stimulus: Evaluate the applicable chain boundary and inspect the resulting determination record before the materially affected execution, verification or claim-scope state is relied upon.
ExpectedSystemBehaviour: An explicit chain-boundary determination is recorded and remains identifiable before the materially affected execution, verification or claim-scope consequence is treated as governed. The record preserves the applicable boundary decision and its relationship to the affected downstream context.
RequiredEvidence: Chain context; boundary inputs; chain-boundary determination record; affected execution, verification or claim-scope context; relationship between the boundary determination and affected context; inspection record.
FailureOracle: FAIL if a material chain boundary affects execution, verification or claim scope without an explicit recorded boundary determination, if the boundary is left only implicit, or if the required determination is retrospectively reconstructed after the affected downstream state.
Notes: Controlled successor definition arising from human semantic review of LILP-REQ-CHAIN-005. Explicit chain-boundary recording remains distinct from generic determination/execution separation, changed-determination history, bypass restraint, ambiguous-determination failure handling and successor preservation. Definition existence does not establish requirement mapping, harness binding, execution or conformance.

Title: ALLOW permits bounded progression without bypassing later execution predicates
Objective: Establish the normative semantics of ALLOW: an applicable ALLOW determination permits progression only within its declared governance scope and does not itself constitute permission to skip, satisfy or bypass later mandatory execution predicates.
Preconditions: A valid governing state supports an ALLOW determination for a declared bounded scope, and one or more later execution predicates remain independently applicable before consequential execution.
Stimulus: Produce the ALLOW determination, permit the bounded governed progression it authorises, then evaluate the later execution stage without treating ALLOW as satisfaction of the independently required execution predicates.
ExpectedSystemBehaviour: ALLOW permits progression only within the declared scope for which it was determined. No consequential execution is inferred from ALLOW alone. All later mandatory execution predicates remain independently required and must be evaluated before execution may proceed.
RequiredEvidence: ALLOW determination; declared scope; governing-state basis; progression record; later mandatory execution predicates; execution-gate or equivalent evaluation record; execution status.
FailureOracle: FAIL if ALLOW is treated as broader authority than its declared scope, if ALLOW itself is treated as completed or permitted consequential execution, or if any later mandatory execution predicate is skipped, presumed satisfied or bypassed solely because ALLOW exists.
Notes: Controlled successor definition arising from human semantic review of LILP-REQ-DET-002. The test isolates the semantic boundary of ALLOW itself: bounded governance progression without conversion into execution authority. It remains distinct from generic determination/execution separation and from the later pre-execution gate tests that evaluate mandatory execution predicates. Definition existence does not establish requirement mapping, harness binding, execution or conformance.

Title: Determination is attributable to governing state and relied-upon evidence
Objective: Establish that every governance determination preserves an inspectable attribution to the governing state and material evidence on which that determination relied.
Preconditions: A consequential governance request has an identifiable governing state, material evidence set and sufficient basis to produce a governance determination.
Stimulus: Produce the governance determination and independently inspect its recorded basis, governing-state reference and relied-upon evidence references.
ExpectedSystemBehaviour: The determination remains explicitly attributable to the governing state under which it was made and to the material evidence actually relied upon. The governing-state and evidence references are identifiable and inspectable without inferring or reconstructing the determination basis from unrelated later state.
RequiredEvidence: Determination record; governing-state object or stable governing-state reference; relied-upon evidence objects or stable evidence references; determination basis; inspection record.
FailureOracle: FAIL if the determination cannot be attributed to the governing state on which it relied, if relied-upon material evidence cannot be identified, or if the claimed determination basis depends on unsupported inference or substitution.
Notes: Controlled successor definition arising from human semantic review of LILP-REQ-DET-001. This test isolates positive determination-basis attribution to governing state and relied-upon evidence. It remains distinct from determination/execution separation, chain-boundary recording and ALLOW semantics. Definition existence does not establish requirement mapping, harness binding, execution or conformance.

Title: Execution gate preserves complete material decision evidence
Objective: Establish that the execution gate produces or causes preservation of sufficient evidence to determine what mandatory predicates were evaluated, what values were observed, what determination resulted, whether execution occurred and what consequence, if any, was established.
Preconditions: A consequential request reaches the execution gate with an identifiable set of applicable mandatory predicates, observable predicate values and a downstream execution and consequence state capable of being recorded or explicitly left unresolved.
Stimulus: Evaluate the execution gate for the consequential request, complete or withhold downstream execution as governed, then inspect the evidence preserved by or through the gate process.
ExpectedSystemBehaviour: The preserved gate evidence is sufficient to identify the predicates evaluated, their observed values, the resulting determination, execution status and consequence status where applicable. Unexecuted, unavailable or unestablished downstream states remain explicitly distinguishable rather than being omitted or inferred as success.
RequiredEvidence: Applicable predicate set; observed predicate values; gate evaluation record; resulting determination; execution status; consequence status or explicit bounded unresolved state; references linking the evidence to the governed request; inspection record.
FailureOracle: FAIL if the preserved gate evidence cannot establish any required material element: predicates evaluated, values observed, resulting determination, execution occurrence or consequence status where applicable; or if a missing element is silently inferred or manufactured.
Notes: Controlled successor definition arising from human semantic review of LILP-REQ-GATE-006. This test isolates the execution-gate evidence-preservation obligation and does not collapse generic gate evaluation, consequence verification or receipt binding into the same test. Definition existence does not establish requirement mapping, harness binding, execution or conformance.

Title: HOLD preserves non-execution while required governance basis remains unresolved
Objective: Establish the normative semantics of HOLD: where required information, authority, governing state or evidence remains unresolved, the HOLD determination preserves non-execution for the contemplated consequential action.
Preconditions: A consequential governance request reaches determination while at least one required information, authority, governing-state or evidence condition remains unresolved and no separately established basis permits consequential execution.
Stimulus: Produce the applicable governance determination while the required condition remains unresolved, then inspect the determination and downstream execution state without supplying the unresolved requirement.
ExpectedSystemBehaviour: The determination remains HOLD while the required governance basis remains unresolved, and consequential execution remains withheld. HOLD does not silently convert unresolved information, authority, state or evidence into an established predicate and does not imply DENY where prohibition has not independently been established.
RequiredEvidence: HOLD determination; unresolved information, authority, governing-state or evidence condition; determination basis; execution state showing non-execution; timestamps or applicable state references.
FailureOracle: FAIL if consequential execution proceeds while the HOLD basis remains unresolved, if HOLD is treated as satisfying the unresolved requirement, or if the system silently converts HOLD into another determination without a separately supported governance basis.
Notes: Controlled successor definition arising from human semantic review of LILP-REQ-DET-003. The test isolates HOLD semantics: unresolved governance basis preserves non-execution. It remains distinct from generic determination/execution separation, missing or ambiguous determination handling, ALLOW semantics and determination-basis attribution. Definition existence does not establish requirement mapping, harness binding, execution or conformance.

Title: DENY represents established prohibition within declared governance scope
Objective: Establish the normative semantics of DENY: the determination represents an established prohibition applicable within the declared governance scope and remains distinguishable from unresolved uncertainty, HOLD or mere absence of execution permission.
Preconditions: A consequential governance request is evaluated within an identifiable governance scope and sufficient governing state, policy, authority and evidence exist to establish a prohibition applicable to the contemplated action.
Stimulus: Produce the applicable governance determination and independently inspect the prohibition basis, declared scope and downstream execution state.
ExpectedSystemBehaviour: The determination is DENY only where the applicable prohibition is established within the declared governance scope. The prohibition basis and scope remain identifiable, consequential execution is not authorised, and unresolved or merely absent permission is not silently represented as DENY.
RequiredEvidence: DENY determination; established prohibition basis; governing policy or rule; declared governance scope; material governing-state and evidence references; execution state; inspection record.
FailureOracle: FAIL if DENY is produced without an established prohibition, if the prohibition is not applicable within the declared governance scope, or if unresolved uncertainty, HOLD or absence of permission is silently represented as DENY.
Notes: Controlled successor definition arising from human semantic review of LILP-REQ-DET-004. The test isolates DENY semantics as established prohibition within declared governance scope. It remains distinct from HOLD, ALLOW, NOT_ESTABLISHED and generic determination/execution separation. Definition existence does not establish requirement mapping, harness binding, execution or conformance.

Title: ESCALATE references separately authorised process without itself granting execution authority
Objective: Establish the normative semantics of ESCALATE: the determination identifies or references a separately authorised process while remaining distinct from execution authority unless the governing policy explicitly establishes such authority.
Preconditions: A consequential governance request has a valid basis for escalation and an identifiable separately authorised escalation process. No execution authority is assumed merely from the existence of the escalation determination.
Stimulus: Produce the ESCALATE determination, inspect the referenced escalation process and its authorisation basis, then inspect whether any consequential execution authority has independently been established.
ExpectedSystemBehaviour: ESCALATE identifies or references a separately authorised process. The escalation determination does not itself grant consequential execution authority unless the applicable governing policy explicitly establishes that authority. Escalation routing and execution authority remain independently inspectable.
RequiredEvidence: ESCALATE determination; escalation-process identifier or reference; evidence that the referenced process is separately authorised; applicable governing policy; execution-authority state; execution state; inspection record.
FailureOracle: FAIL if ESCALATE does not identify or reference a separately authorised process, or if the escalation determination itself is treated as granting consequential execution authority without explicit governing-policy support.
Notes: Controlled successor definition arising from human semantic review of LILP-REQ-DET-005. The test isolates ESCALATE semantics and the separation between escalation routing and execution authority. It remains distinct from ALLOW, HOLD, DENY and generic determination/execution separation. Definition existence does not establish requirement mapping, harness binding, execution or conformance.

Title: INVALID remains distinguishable from NOT_ESTABLISHED
Objective: Establish that INVALID and NOT_ESTABLISHED remain distinct determination states: an object, proposition or determination that fails an applicable validity criterion is not silently treated as merely unresolved, and an unresolved basis is not silently treated as established invalidity.
Preconditions: Two bounded governance evaluation cases are available under an identifiable governing context: one case has a directly inspectable basis for failing an applicable validity criterion, while the second lacks sufficient established basis for the required proposition but does not independently establish that the proposition or object is invalid.
Stimulus: Evaluate both bounded cases under the applicable governance rules and inspect the resulting determination state, supporting basis and downstream non-execution state without repairing, substituting or supplying missing evidence.
ExpectedSystemBehaviour: The case with an established validity failure is represented as INVALID when that determination is supported by the applicable governing rule. The unresolved case remains NOT_ESTABLISHED where the required basis cannot be established. INVALID and NOT_ESTABLISHED remain separately attributable and are not substituted for one another solely because both prevent unsupported consequential progression.
RequiredEvidence: Applicable validity criterion or rule; evidence establishing the validity failure for the INVALID case; unresolved or insufficient basis for the NOT_ESTABLISHED case; resulting determination states; governing-context references; execution state; timestamps or equivalent inspection record.
FailureOracle: FAIL if an unresolved basis is represented as INVALID without an established validity failure, if an established validity failure is silently represented only as NOT_ESTABLISHED, or if the implementation cannot preserve an inspectable distinction between INVALID and NOT_ESTABLISHED.
Notes: Controlled successor definition arising from Batch 001R human semantic review of LILP-REQ-DET-007. The test isolates the required distinction between INVALID and NOT_ESTABLISHED. Definition existence does not establish requirement mapping, harness binding, execution, result or conformance.

Title: Material claim identifies claim class or unambiguously identifies claimed property
Objective: Establish that every material claim identifies its claim class or otherwise makes the specific property being claimed unambiguous, so that the claim cannot silently shift between materially different claim meanings.
Preconditions: A material claim is available with an associated evidence basis, evaluated property and declared context. The claim representation can be inspected independently of undocumented author intent.
Stimulus: Inspect the material claim and determine whether it explicitly identifies its claim class or otherwise represents the claimed property with sufficient specificity to distinguish it from materially different claim properties.
ExpectedSystemBehaviour: The material claim explicitly identifies its claim class or unambiguously identifies the property being claimed. The claim meaning remains inspectable from the governed claim representation and does not depend on unstated assumptions, surrounding implication or retrospective interpretation to determine what property was asserted.
RequiredEvidence: Material claim; claim-class identifier where used; explicit claimed-property representation where claim class is not used; evaluated property; evidence basis; declared context; inspection record.
FailureOracle: FAIL if a material claim neither identifies its claim class nor makes the claimed property unambiguous, if materially different claim meanings remain plausible from the governed representation, or if the claimed property can only be established through undocumented or retrospective interpretation.
Notes: Controlled successor definition arising from Batch 001S human semantic review of LILP-REQ-CLAIM-001. The test isolates claim-class or equivalent claimed-property identification. It remains distinct from evidence sufficiency, claim scope, independent-verification prerequisites, profile completeness and conformance-status assignment. Definition existence does not establish requirement mapping, harness binding, execution, result or conformance.

Title: Claim identifies the subject to which it applies
Objective: Establish that a claim identifies the subject to which the claimed property applies, preserving attribution between the assertion and the specific system, object, component, process, profile, evidence package or other declared subject.
Preconditions: A claim exists concerning a bounded subject and claimed property. The subject can be independently identified within the governed context and is distinguishable from other possible subjects.
Stimulus: Inspect the claim representation and determine whether the subject to which the claim applies is explicitly identified or otherwise unambiguously bound to the claim.
ExpectedSystemBehaviour: The claim identifies or unambiguously binds the subject to which it applies. The claimed property cannot silently transfer to another system, object, component, process, profile, evidence package or other subject merely because that subject appears in the same context.
RequiredEvidence: Claim; subject identifier or unambiguous subject binding; claimed property; declared context; relevant evidence or provenance reference; inspection record.
FailureOracle: FAIL if the subject of the claim is absent or materially ambiguous, if multiple materially different subjects could reasonably receive the claim, or if the claimed property can be silently attributed to a different subject without a separately established claim.
Notes: Controlled successor definition arising from Batch 001S human semantic review of LILP-REQ-CLAIM-002. The test isolates claim-subject identification and attribution. Claim subject remains distinct from claim class, claimed property, evaluated scope and evidence sufficiency. Definition existence does not establish requirement mapping, harness binding, execution, result or conformance.

Title: Time-sensitive claim identifies its temporal scope
Objective: Establish that where time materially affects the validity of a claim, the claim identifies the temporal scope within which the claimed property is asserted to hold.
Preconditions: A material claim concerns a property whose validity can materially vary with time, state epoch, effective period, observation time or other temporally bounded condition. The supporting evidence and applicable temporal context are inspectable.
Stimulus: Inspect the governed claim representation and determine whether it identifies the applicable temporal scope or otherwise unambiguously binds the claimed property to the relevant time, period, epoch or temporal condition.
ExpectedSystemBehaviour: Where time materially affects validity, the claim identifies or unambiguously preserves its temporal scope. The claim does not silently present a historically valid, future-valid, expired or otherwise time-bounded property as timeless or currently valid outside the supported temporal scope.
RequiredEvidence: Claim; claimed property; temporal-scope identifier or unambiguous temporal binding; relevant timestamps, effective period, state epoch or time-sensitive condition; supporting evidence; applicable status; inspection record.
FailureOracle: FAIL if time materially affects claim validity and the claim omits or materially obscures its temporal scope, if a historically or otherwise temporally bounded property is silently represented as timeless or current, or if the applicable temporal scope can only be reconstructed retrospectively from information not preserved in the governed claim representation.
Notes: Controlled successor definition arising from Batch 001T human semantic review of LILP-REQ-CLAIM-004. The test isolates temporal claim-scope identification where time materially affects validity. It remains distinct from general claim scope and changed-condition reassessment. Definition existence does not establish requirement mapping, harness binding, execution, result or conformance.

Title: Conformance claim identifies exact standard version and profile
Objective: Establish that every conformance claim identifies the exact standard version and conformance profile relied upon, so that the claimed conformance basis is bounded, reproducible and not silently transferred across different standard versions or profiles.
Preconditions: A conformance claim is available. The governing standard has an identifiable version and the applicable conformance profile is identifiable and distinguishable from other versions or profiles.
Stimulus: Inspect the governed conformance claim and determine whether it explicitly identifies the exact standard version and the specific conformance profile on which the claim relies.
ExpectedSystemBehaviour: The conformance claim explicitly identifies or unambiguously binds both the exact standard version and the conformance profile relied upon. The claim cannot silently inherit, substitute or transfer conformance across a different standard version, profile or unspecified conformance basis.
RequiredEvidence: Conformance claim; exact standard identifier and version; conformance-profile identifier; applicable profile definition; claim scope; supporting requirements-matrix or determination evidence; inspection record.
FailureOracle: FAIL if a conformance claim omits or materially ambiguates the standard version or conformance profile relied upon, if more than one materially different version or profile could support the wording, or if the claim can be transferred to another version or profile without a separately established conformance basis.
Notes: Controlled successor definition arising from Batch 001V human semantic review of LILP-REQ-CLAIM-008. The test isolates exact standard-version and conformance-profile identification in the claim itself. It remains distinct from requirements-matrix completeness within an already declared profile. Definition existence does not establish requirement mapping, harness binding, execution, result or conformance.

Title: PL3 identifies the procedure and evidence used
Objective: Establish that a PL3 proof-level claim or governed PL3 record identifies both the procedure relied upon and the evidence used to support the claimed result.
Preconditions: A PL3 claim or governed PL3 determination exists; a procedure was relied upon for the bounded evaluated property; and an evidence set was used in reaching the PL3 claim or determination.
Stimulus: Inspect the PL3 claim or governed PL3 record and determine whether the relied-upon procedure and the evidence used are each explicitly identified or otherwise unambiguously bound to the PL3 representation.
ExpectedSystemBehaviour: The PL3 representation identifies or unambiguously binds both the procedure relied upon and the evidence used. Procedure identity and evidence identity remain separately inspectable, and neither is silently inferred from an undocumented process, surrounding context or retrospective reconstruction.
RequiredEvidence: PL3 claim or determination; bounded evaluated property; procedure identifier or unambiguous procedure reference; evidence identifiers or evidence-set reference; applicable result; provenance; inspection record.
FailureOracle: FAIL if PL3 is positively represented while the procedure used is absent or materially ambiguous, the evidence used is absent or materially ambiguous, either can only be reconstructed retrospectively from information not preserved in the governed PL3 representation, or the representation cannot distinguish the relied-upon procedure from the supporting evidence.
Notes: Controlled successor definition arising from Batch 001W human semantic review of LILP-REQ-PROOF-005. The test isolates PL3 procedure-and-evidence identification. It remains distinct from generic evidence-basis traceability and from withholding a positive claim where the required proof level cannot be established. Definition existence does not establish requirement mapping, harness binding, execution, result or conformance.

Title: PL5 identifies reproduction conditions and result
Objective: Establish that a PL5 proof-level claim or governed PL5 record identifies both the reproduction conditions under which the evaluated property was reproduced and the result obtained under those conditions.
Preconditions: A PL5 claim or governed PL5 determination exists; a bounded evaluated property has been subjected to reproduction; the relevant reproduction conditions are knowable; and a reproduction result exists.
Stimulus: Inspect the PL5 claim or governed PL5 record and determine whether the reproduction conditions and the resulting outcome are each explicitly identified or otherwise unambiguously bound to the PL5 representation.
ExpectedSystemBehaviour: The PL5 representation identifies or unambiguously binds both the reproduction conditions and the result obtained under those conditions. The conditions and result remain separately inspectable and preserve the bounded circumstances under which reproduction occurred, without silently generalising the result beyond those conditions.
RequiredEvidence: PL5 claim or determination; bounded evaluated property; reproduction-condition identifiers or complete bounded condition description; reproduced result; applicable procedure or method reference where preserved; supporting evidence; provenance; inspection record.
FailureOracle: FAIL if PL5 is positively represented while the reproduction conditions are absent or materially ambiguous, the result is absent or materially ambiguous, the result cannot be bound to the stated reproduction conditions, the conditions or result can only be reconstructed retrospectively from information not preserved in the governed PL5 representation, or the reproduced result is silently represented as applying beyond the conditions under which it was obtained.
Notes: Controlled successor definition arising from Batch 001X human semantic review of LILP-REQ-PROOF-007. The test isolates PL5 reproduction-condition and result identification. It remains distinct from PL3 procedure-and-evidence identification, generic evidence-basis traceability, and independent-verification prerequisites. Definition existence does not establish requirement mapping, harness binding, execution, result or conformance.
